terms.meaning: the library the app uses to talk to its database

sections.name: File setup, insertEvent
sections.title: Saving an event
sections.what: Writes one analytics event row to the database and returns only its ID.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps database writes in one place so the service does not touch the database directly.

sections.name: eventsUntil, hasEvent
sections.title: Reading events and checking one
sections.what: Loads every event before a cutoff date, oldest first, for the weekly reports. Also counts whether a user already has an event with a given name.
sections.why: Likely reason: the weekly measures need full history, so the read is not limited to a short window.
sections.watch_out: Loading every event before a date gets slower as the log grows, and there is no paging.

summary: Saves analytics events and reads them back for reports.
purpose: The database layer for analytics events.
why: Likely reason: keeps reads and writes of events in one place.
how: 1. Save an event row and return its ID. 2. Load all events before a cutoff date, oldest first. 3. Check whether a user already has an event with a given name.
inputs: A user ID, an event name, event details, and dates.
outputs: A saved event's ID, a list of events, or a yes or no answer.
risks: Loading every event before a date becomes slow as the log grows.
debug: If reports are slow, check how many events exist. If one-time events repeat, check the hasEvent answer and the code calling it.
